metadata.remarks:
Tier 3 — High-risk worked example. Selects all 72 controls (include-all) with the explicit framing that AI in regulated or safety-critical contexts (healthcare, finance, government, infrastructure, autonomous transport) requires the full AI RMF surface area. Differs from the baseline profile only in narrative framing. The same selection (all 72 controls) but with the explicit position that exclusions are not appropriate for high-risk deployment contexts. This is a worked example, not a normative baseline. Released under CC0 1.0. Not endorsed by NIST.

PROVENANCE AND DISCLAIMERS:

This profile is a community-authored worked example of an OSCAL Profile
derived from the open Agent Threat Rules (ATR) community-contributed AI RMF
catalog. It is NOT authored by NIST, NOT endorsed by NIST, and NOT a NIST
publication. Any consumer should treat this artifact as community output and
NOT as authoritative AI RMF baseline guidance.

The NIST AI RMF Core (NIST AI 100-1) remains the authoritative source for
the AI Risk Management Framework. The NIST OSCAL Team is the authoritative
source for any official OSCAL representation of the AI RMF, when such an
artifact is published. The OSCAL representation of the AI RMF is currently
on hold at NIST per usnistgov/OSCAL#2234.

Provenance:
- Upstream catalog: github.com/Agent-Threat-Rule/ai-rmf-oscal-catalog (CC0 1.0)
- Profile author: ATR community (NOT NIST)
- Profile license: CC0 1.0 (public domain)
- This vendored copy: usnistgov/oscal-content/src/examples/profile/...
- Sync workflow: .github/workflows/community-ai-rmf-atr-sync.yml
- Tracking issue: usnistgov/OSCAL#2234

PROFILE RESOLUTION SPECIFICATION KNOWN-EDGE-CASE AUDIT:

The OSCAL Profile Resolution Specification has the following open issues at
the time of authoring this profile (verified against the live tracker on
2026-05-11). Each is checked against this profile and the imported catalog
to confirm it does not affect resolved-catalog correctness:

1. usnistgov/OSCAL#2233 ('Profile Resolution "As-Is" Can Yield Invalid
   Catalogs'): This profile uses 'include-controls' import-type, not the
   'as-is' import behaviour described in the issue. Verified not applicable.

2. usnistgov/OSCAL#2231 ('No Provision for Group ID Collision in Profile
   Syntax or Profile Resolution'): The imported catalog uses unique group
   IDs (ai-rmf-gv, ai-rmf-mp, ai-rmf-ms, ai-rmf-mg at top level, with
   numbered subgroups ai-rmf-gv-1 through ai-rmf-mg-4). No collision risk
   from this profile's include selection.

3. usnistgov/OSCAL#2166 ('Profile resolution test for merge functionality
   fails.'): This profile uses 'merge.flat' (the simplest merge mode) and
   does not depend on 'merge.combine' behaviour where the issue surfaces.
   Verified not applicable to this profile's resolved-catalog output.

4. usnistgov/OSCAL#1314 ('Profile resolution: clarification needed wrt
   pruning'): This profile uses explicit include-all OR explicit 'with-ids'
   selection of named controls. No pruning ambiguity arises because every
   selected control is fully retained.

This audit is the result of the profile author having read the issue
descriptions and traced each against this profile's import + include
behaviour. Any change to the upstream catalog or this profile's include
selection invalidates this audit; the sync workflow at
.github/workflows/community-ai-rmf-atr-sync.yml regenerates this audit
when either is modified.
